liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): The show opens with China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider; Reviewer specifically remembers China Cat Sunflower from the show [13][18]
- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Sugaree opens a lucid, emotional second set; Reviewer liked Sugaree opening the second set [13][19]
- **China Doll** (1 review): Garcia sings the 'take up your china doll' line at half tempo, nearly stopping the song and stunning the band [14]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): A strong, steady breeze blew on the band during Rider, which the reviewer recalls as a notable slip [16]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): A train passed in the background during Big Railroad Blues [19]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Garcia plays a hot, ripping solo section on The Music Never Stopped [22]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): The Playin' jam locks into the slipstream; the band played after a month-long layoff [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd83-07-30 01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 02 China Cat Sunflower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 03 I Know You Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 04 It's All Over Now**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 05 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 06 My Brother Esau**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 07 Big Railroad Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd83-07-30 08 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-07-30.140317.sbd.eaton.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: There is some distortion in Weir's vocal microphone [1]
- **gd1983-07-30.179164.neumann.km84i.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 146 min [2]
- **gd1983-07-30.167231.nak100.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 149 min [4]
- **gd1983-07-30.fob.sony220t.keshavan.miller.96401.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 144 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the Keshavan Sony audience recording superb [24]
- **gd1983-07-30.150940.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: source not stated; 18 songs; 151 min [7]
- **gd83-07-30.aud.dodd.11932.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 138 min; rated 3.58/5 by 12 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the audience recording spectacular, made on a breezy Southern California day; The audience recording has a lot of wind noise [13][23]

## Around the show

- A sunny 78-degree day, with dancers on a dusty rodeo floor and mass skinny-dipping in the ocean at sunset afterward [16]
- Reviewer recalls Garcia staring at the ground, looking gray, fumbling lyrics and playing with unsteady tempos in summer 1983 [17]
- A dusty, windy daytime setting by the beach; wind disturbed the live sound and the tapes [18]
- A windy dustbowl with palm trees; reviewer calls Ventura a West Coast must, usually ending a tour swing [19]
- The trip took an hour longer than expected, parking was far away in dust, and dirt swirled through the venue [21]
- A biplane flew behind the stage during the daytime show [21]
- Very hot even for Southern California, with a hot wind blowing dirt and dust; reviewer got heat stroke [23]
- Reviewer finds it less fun than the great shows at the same beach venue the year before [14]
- Reviewer says the wind problem also happened at the first Ventura show [18]
- Reviewer calls it a sleeper show that starts roughly but grows into something much stronger [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-07-30.140317.sbd.eaton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Cassette -> Technics Reel to Reel -> Panasonic SV-3800 Dat 16/48 [1]. Also: Soundboard from Rob Eaton's DAT source, transferred by Charlie Miller; the first soundboard in circulation for this date, December 2017; The Sony 220t audience source supplies some crowd sound and the first few seconds of Brown Eyed Women [1]
- **gd1983-07-30.179164.neumann.km84i.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes: Neumann KM84i mics (mounted in an x/y pattern on a 12' pole) > Sony D5M > Bill Bradt's 1st generation cassettes(TDK MA-90) [2]. Also: A 5:19 patch in Drums combines the Sony ECM 220t source with Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source [2]
- **gd1983-07-30.167231.nak100.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ken Kelley; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ken Kelley's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 100 mics > JVC KD-2 w/Super ANRS (Maxell XLII-S90) [4]. Also: Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 0:25 patch in the Cassidy to Loser transition; A 5:10 patch in Drums combines Keshavan's Sony ECM 220t and Wagner's Nakamichi 700 sources [4]
- **gd1983-07-30.fob.sony220t.keshavan.miller.96401.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rango Keshavan; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-220T -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Fuji Metal Tape/Dolby B) [6]
- **gd1983-07-30.150940.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M [7]
- **gd83-07-30.aud.dodd.11932.sbeok.shnf**: source: ACM>DAT>CDR [10]
